facility_roles.quote: Here we present results from an expedition to the north-eastern region of the South China Sea, in the western Pacific Ocean.

intervals.label: proposed (design paper and pathfinder results)
intervals.locator: arXiv abstract page of the design paper (Nature Astronomy 7, 1497 (2023))
intervals.note: Start is the arXiv submission month of the design paper. The paper schedules a 10-string pilot project at the selected site for about 2026 and construction of the full array after a successful demonstration; no source seen reports that either has started, so no construction interval is entered.

quantity.quote: The detector contains 1211 strings, each containing 20 hDOMs separated vertically by 30 m
This arrangement will result in a world-leading instrumented geometric volume of ∼ 7.5 km3
A favorable neutrino telescope site was found on an abyssal plain at a depth of ∼ 3.5 km.

name: TRIDENT
notes: No official TRIDENT website was consulted; none recorded.
The design paper schedules a 10-string pilot at the site for ~2026; whether it has been deployed was not found.

physics_goals.quote: TRIDENT expects to observe the IceCube steady source candidate NGC 1068 with 5$\sigma$ significance within 1 year of operation.
physics_goals.value: Observe the sources of the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux from a site near the equator, e.g. the IceCube steady-source candidate NGC 1068 within one year of operation

summary.plain: A proposed neutrino telescope in the South China Sea: over a thousand strings of light sensors hanging 3 kilometres deep, filling several cubic kilometres of seawater, to spot cosmic neutrinos from near the equator. A pathfinder has measured the clarity of the water at the chosen site.
summary.technical: TRopIcal DEep-sea Neutrino Telescope: 1211 strings x 20 hybrid optical modules (multi-PMT with SiPMs, 30 m spacing, 2800-3400 m depth, Penrose-tiling layout) for ~7.5 km^3 instrumented volume at an abyssal-plain site near 114.0 E, 17.4 N; T-REX pathfinder measured absorption length ~27 m, scattering length ~63 m, current speed < 10 cm/s; 5 sigma on NGC 1068 in one year expected.
